claims.text: Ethiopia- Expressway Development Support Project (P148850) is the closest comparable: same country, same sector, similar description and size. It is closed, with commitment of USD 297,920,032 and 43 contract awards, and has no outcome rating.

Ethiopia: Transport Systems Improvement Project (TRANSIP, P151819), Road Sector Support Project (P131118) and Ethiopia Rural Connectivity to Support Food Security Program (P176303) match on country, sector and size. P151819 was rated Moderately Unsatisfactory.
Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (P164336) is comparable by description and size but sits in agriculture, not transport. It had 719 contract awards, so it is a weaker comparator for road works.

Road rehabilitation works: the model estimates 211 days from tender to signing (likely range 97-468), with a 22% chance of exceeding a year. Estimated signing date is 2028-04-29. This is a model estimate, not a recorded fact.

Construction supervision (Individual Consultant Selection suggested): the model estimates 190 days (likely range 88-423), with an 18% chance of exceeding a year. Estimated signing date is 2028-02-07. This is a model estimate.

Estimated drivers for the works package: approval year shortens the tender, while the 45-day bid window and project age at tender lengthen it. The procurement plan should treat the signing dates as estimates and allow for the upper range, with supervision signing before works.
For Works in ET since FY2016, Request for Bids was used in 556 awards (median USD 377,350) and Request for Quotations in 488 (median USD 114,353). Review was Post in 1041 awards and Prior in 22.

For Consultant Services in ET since FY2016, Individual Consultant Selection had 349 awards (median USD 12,923) and Quality And Cost-Based Selection 132 (median USD 427,853). Review was Post in 480 awards and Prior in 122.

Supplier origin: 1034 Works awards went entirely to suppliers from the same country and 20 included another country. For Consultant Services, 482 awards were all same-country and 118 included other-country suppliers.

Contract amendment risk for Road rehabilitation works is simulated at 31.6%, placing it on the demonstration review list; the model was trained on synthetic data. Mitigation: put an experienced consultant on contract design and monitoring, as a past appraisal proposed.

Simulated re-bidding risk is low: 7.1% for Road rehabilitation works and 2.7% for Construction supervision. Simulated amendment risk for supervision is 14.9%, not on the review list. These models were trained on synthetic data.

Governance context is moderate: 2025 CPIA overall 3.25, transparency and corruption 3.0, WGI government effectiveness -0.62. A past appraisal rated transport ministry staff capacity as a high risk, mitigated by assigning a qualified full-time procurement specialist experienced in Bank procurement.

Ethiopian procurement plans report that gaps in standard performance and compliance specifications caused many clarifications and addenda, delaying procedures. Do differently: finalise specifications and bidding documents before the tender dates.

An appraisal of Ethiopian power utility projects recorded poor quality specifications, designs and bidding documents, with higher costs and reduced competition. Do differently: complete designs before bidding and check the roads authority's procurement staffing.

A completed Ethiopian program credited structured, systematic capacity building across government levels, with well-trained staff and focal persons. Do the same for the regional roads authority's maintenance capacity building.

A prior hybrid operation's design lessons were to include capacity building for the agencies and to rely on consultation with central, regional and local governments. Do differently: consult regional and local bodies in Oromia during preparation.

The 45-day bid window is a modelled driver lengthening the works tender. Prior review is rare for Works in ET (22 awards), so allow time for reviews. Check the bid window against how complete the bidding documents are.

Confirm the supervision selection method before finalising: the model assumed Individual Consultant Selection (median USD 12,923), while Quality And Cost-Based Selection has a median of USD 427,853. Match the method to the scope.

For the Road Authority's procurement experience, a past appraisal noted most of 29 design-and-build contracts used open tender, most under US$70 million. Use this when setting qualification thresholds for rehabilitation lots and bridges.

Track tender durations against the model estimates: works 211 days and supervision 190 days. Treat movement toward the upper likely bounds (468 and 423 days) as an early warning to revise the procurement plan signing dates.
Watch for bidder clarification requests and addenda on specifications, and for variations, weak dispute resolution and staff turnover. Past appraisals link these to delays and corruption risk.

limitations: Tender duration figures are model estimates, not recorded outcomes; test error is about 77 days.
Amendment and re-bidding risk models were trained on synthetic data and are not validated World Bank risk accuracy.
Country-level medians from approval to signing are much longer than the model's tender-to-signing estimates and measure a different interval.
Several document passages are truncated, and some appraisal tables are unverified, so only qualitative points were used from them.
Only a few similar projects have documents available; no evidence covers Oromia roads or bridges specifically.
PDF table values are cited for context only; they are not verified figures.
Amendment and re-bidding risks come from models trained on synthetic data; they are not validated World Bank risk estimates.

view.message: The project appraisal document for the road project records that many road construction projects experience delays and cost overruns because of poor design work and contract administration by consultants, and because contractors are slow to mobilize. The same document identifies procurement delays at the roads agency as a key risk. The stated causes are non-standard bidding documents, a long evaluation caused by the two-envelope system, and slow approvals from a long iterative process. A risk table in the document adds that there were no standard bidding documents for Design and Build works. This led to protracted preparation and approval and to many clarification requests from bidders. It also notes that bids were evaluated slowly because of the two-envelope system and differences between design-and-build bids, and that report quality was below standard. The recorded lesson is to adopt a Design and Build contract format to address delays and cost overruns from poor design, weak contract administration and late mobilization. The agreed response to procurement delays was for the roads agency to strengthen its internal quality assurance so that it submits quality procurement documents. The agency and the Bank also agreed business standards for responding to comments and agreed to meet to resolve outstanding issues after the agency's second submission. The proposed mitigation was to customise bid documents from pre-approved Output Performance Road Contract documents, prepared and agreed before negotiations. It also included training the evaluation team and providing technical assistance support. In a water supply and sanitation works procurement plan for the Afar region, the contract was signed later than planned, on 2023-04-04 against a planned date of 2023-03-06. The record gives no cause for the difference.
